requirement.description: Validate/challenge 4 conclusions from full backtest analysis of 3-subsystem fusion trading platform. Conclusions: (1) LY walk-forward 50.9% OOS=no predictive power, (2) Fusion 55.2% < ML 62.9% because LY drags down, (3) AT 47.0% confirms counter-indicator status, (4) ML 62.9% direction accuracy and 24.68% operation win rate measure different things.

oracle_analysis.root_cause: LY (58.6%) actually BEATS fusion (55.2%) on directional calls — LY is not the drag. Real root cause is weighted averaging produces structurally bearish output under disagreement (ALL 26 disagreement cases → bearish fusion). The 'consensus=reliability' thesis has no empirical support (all-3-agree = 50% accuracy). ml_factor weight (0.06) bug confirmed but minor. Data leak real but negligible (<2% of training).
oracle_analysis.initial_recommendation: Redesign disagreement handling logic (don't penalize score, just cap position). Consider dropping AT weight to 0.05 or 0.0. Give sentiment_score higher blend weight vs operation_advice (not 50/50). Fix ml_factor weight loading in _compute_adjusted_weights. Increase sample size before tuning weights.

c1skill_validation.stage_4_counter_arguments: Sample size too small (150 matched, 14 trading days) for reliable conclusions — 95% CI too wide. Daily accuracy varies from 10% to 89% — aggregate masks variance. Stock-specific accuracy varies 58-81% — one-size-fits-all weights are suboptimal. The flat zone filtering (42-52% → neutral) is a legitimate post-processing improvement, not cheating.
c1skill_validation.stage_7_final_conclusion: 4 conclusions directionally correct but miss deeper mechanism. Fusion underperformance is NOT because LY drags ML down — it's because weighted averaging creates degenerate bearish output under any disagreement. Confidence intervals too wide for decisive action; collect more data.

final_outcome.patch_summary: No code changes — advisory analysis only. Identified 1 code bug (ml_factor weight omission), 2 design issues (disagreement handling, blend formula), and 1 premise failure (consensus=reliability). Recommended holding system as-is pending more data.
